title: Ida checks the bridge (paraphrase C)
topic: An engineer named Ida inspects an old road bridge, finds a crack in the concrete and explains the delay to waiting drivers

notes: Formulation C: third independent re-phrasing of the ten F05A meaning units in both languages (same events, same order, same name Ida). Replacements include inspects in the early morning/checks at daybreak (prüft am frühen Morgen/kontrolliert bei Tagesanbruch), walks across with a notebook/strides across notebook in hand (läuft über/schreitet über, mit einem Notizbuch/mit dem Notizbuch in der Hand), steel beams carry heavy trucks every day/steel supports hold heavy lorries every single day (Stahlträger tragen/Stahlstützen halten), worker lowers a camera/assistant sends a camera (Arbeiter senkt/Gehilfe schickt), screen shows/display detects (Bildschirm zeigt/Display erfasst), measures the crack with a ruler/checks the crack's length with a ruler (misst den Riss/prüft die Länge des Risses), cars form a long line at the barrier/a queue of cars builds up at the roadblock (Autos bilden eine Schlange an der Absperrung/Autoschlange bildet sich an der Straßensperre), asks about the delay through his window/queries the hold-up through the open window (fragt nach der Verzögerung durch sein Fenster/fragt wegen der Verspätung durch das offene Fenster), explains in a calm voice/outlines in a calm tone (erklärt mit ruhiger Stimme/erläutert in ruhigem Ton), inspection ends shortly before noon/inspection concludes just before midday (Inspektion endet kurz vor Mittag/Begehung endet knapp vor Mittag). 'traffic' and 'Verkehr' are absent. 'bildet sich' is reflexive; 'erläutert' and 'erfasst' are inseparable; no separable verbs. Present tense and positive polarity throughout. Unit 9 reads naturally in German; units 1 and 10 read naturally in English.
